column3: The immediately preceding rebuke names worship besides God, supplying the offense whose consequence the focus declares.
The scene of cast hearing and falsehood does not clarify the focus's worship-and-Fire relation.
Exclusive worship of God and warning of painful punishment provide the positive command and its threatened alternative.
It repeats the focus's pairing of worshippers with what they worship, making the shared-subject construction explicit.
The nearby record of believing righteous action offers only broad local contrast to the condemned group.
Withdrawal from those who worship otherwise than God gives a concrete separation from the relation condemned in the focus.
God alone can remove the coming event, a limited counterpart to the focus's final consequence.
The immediately approaching apocalypse supplies the local eschatological setting into which the focus's warning arrives.
Its command to worship God alone supplies a general contrary orientation.
Its use of "besides" concerns a different moral comparison, not worship or the Fire.
It immediately tests the alleged divinity of the worshipped objects by their joint entry and abiding in the Fire.

The designation of Noah as a believing servant does not add beyond a general contrast.

The designation of Elijah as a believing servant adds only a broad contrast.
Universal arrival at the Fire provides an important but qualified parallel to the focus's specific entry warning.

The awaited single blast does not clarify false worship's shared fate.
The inheritance of the earth by righteous servants is a distant local contrast, not an explanation of the focus's judgment.

Admission to gardens after faithful striving is a secondary contrary outcome to entry into the Fire.

Conflicting speech does not materially add to false worship's fate.

Abraham's declared separation from what his people worship gives a direct contrary stance.
The opening and withholding of mercy do not explain the focus's worship-and-Fire relation.
The believers' prayer and desire to die with the righteous do not materially add to the focus.
Thankful worship of God provides a general contrary use of worship.
The recognition of unfamiliar visitors is unrelated to the focus.
Universal mercy does not clarify the focus's specific judgment.
The question about where the formerly worshipped objects are directly anticipates their inability to answer or save.
The threat of an earthly catastrophe does not clarify the focus's Fire scene.
Revelation to a servant and warning to worlds add no specific relation here.
Abraham's demand to examine what his people worship prepares the scrutiny of false objects in the focus.
The ordered sky is not materially connected to the focus.
The declaration of one God supplies the local contrary claim to worship beside God.
God's knowledge of servants and the revealed Book do not clarify the focus.
The threatened stone storm is a different punishment image.
The division of people into miserable and happy at the coming day gives a broad outcome contrast.
The worshipped parties become enemies and reject their worshippers at the gathering, closely explaining why the relation cannot protect them.
Its catalog of punishments offers only a general judgment parallel.
The nearby warning of what is promised extends the local address without explaining the focus's relation.
The reciprocal refusal of worship marks the enduring incompatibility of the two allegiances.
The stone storm and Lot's rescue are not materially connected to the focus.

The announcement of mercy to God's servants does not clarify the focus's judgment.

Divine knowledge of open and hidden speech does not materially add to the focus.

Gardens and palaces do not clarify the focus.
Reverent servants provide only a broad contrast to those in the focus.

Trial and temporary enjoyment do not clarify the focus.

The closing appeal for judgment by truth does not add to the focus's specific relation.
The inherited commitment to worship one God supplies a monotheistic contrast.

Inheritance rules do not materially add to the focus.
Entry among God's servants is too general to clarify the focus after stronger contrasts.

The description of Jesus as a favored servant does not clarify false worship's fate.
The availability of worldly and final reward does not explain the focus.

The command to worship God alone supplies the contrary allegiance, though its main added concern lies elsewhere.
It describes a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, the closest missing parallel to the focus's fuel image and human entry.
It calls the disbelievers fuel for the Fire, directly paralleling the focus's transformation of worshippers into Fire material.
It makes associating partners with God a cause of exclusion from the Garden and destination in the Fire.
It challenges worship of what has neither power to harm nor benefit, closely supporting the exposure of false objects in the focus.
The gathering scene asks where the alleged partners are, directly anticipating the failure of false worship at judgment.
It forbids worship of those called upon besides God, supplying the focus's prohibited relation in a direct form.
It rejects calling upon what neither benefits nor harms apart from God, closely clarifying the worthlessness of the worshipped objects.
It asks whether people associate beings that create nothing and are themselves created, undermining their claimed divinity.
It states that those called besides God cannot help either their worshippers or themselves.
It identifies worship besides God of what neither harms nor benefits and calls the claimed intercessors into question.
It says the gods invoked besides God did not avail their people when divine judgment came, a close consequence parallel.
It depicts those called besides God as unable to answer their callers, exposing the void in the worship relation.
It condemns setting rivals alongside God and connects that act to being led toward the Fire.
It identifies those invoked besides God as created beings that create nothing.
It rejects worship besides God of beings that possess no provision or power.
At judgment, the associators see their partners and acknowledge that they had been associating them with God.
It challenges worshippers to call those they claim besides God, who cannot remove or redirect harm.
It rebukes taking gods besides God without clear authority, directly naming the contested allegiance.
It describes taking gods besides God in hope of honor, a motive reversed by the focus's humiliation in the Fire.
The idol is burned and scattered, providing a close image of a worshipped object subjected to fire rather than offering protection.
It questions whether earthly gods can raise the dead, exposing the impotence of alleged deities in the focus's local setting.
It argues that multiple gods would corrupt the heavens and earth, supporting the local rejection of rival divinities.
It directly asks whether gods have been taken besides God and demands proof for that claim.
It gives the local positive command: no deity but God, so worship Him alone.
It describes calling upon besides God what can neither harm nor benefit and labels that course far astray.
It shows the caller reaching for one whose harm is nearer than benefit, a close reversal of expected protection.
It condemns invoking another god with God and assigns the final reckoning to the Lord.
It describes adopted gods besides God that neither create nor control harm, benefit, death, life, or resurrection.
It names worship besides God of what neither benefits nor harms, directly matching the false-object side of the focus.
Abraham's question to his people about what they worship opens the sustained examination of their false objects.
The judgment question asks where the objects were that people worshipped besides God.
It says the idols taken among the people will become a source of denial and mutual repudiation on the Day of Resurrection.
It denies that those called besides God possess even the smallest share of power in heaven or earth.
At the gathering, the angels deny that people had worshipped them, closely paralleling the collapse of claimed worship ties.
The angels declare God free of imperfection and identify the worship as directed instead toward jinn.
It denies that those called besides God possess even a date-stone's membrane of sovereignty.
It says those called besides God cannot hear or answer, and will deny their worship on the Day of Resurrection.
It rejects taking gods besides God because their intercession cannot avert harm or save the speaker.
It portrays people taking gods besides God in hope of help, a hope the focus decisively overturns.
It states that the alleged gods cannot help their worshippers, who instead stand as an assembled host for them.
It commands the gathering of wrongdoers together with their associates and what they used to worship, closely matching the focus's joint treatment.
It specifies that the gathered worshipped beings were those worshipped besides God and sends the group toward the Fire's path.
It challenges the worship of things people themselves carve, directly exposing the created status of the objects.
It records worship of protectors besides God as a claimed means of nearness, supplying a direct rival rationale to the focus's verdict.
It asks whether those called besides God can remove harm or withhold mercy, directly testing their protective claim.
It asks the condemned where their former partners are at the point of judgment.
It identifies those missing partners as the beings invoked besides God and records their disappearance from the worshippers.
It denies that those invoked besides God possess intercession, limiting any claim to those who bear witness to truth.
It challenges those who call others besides God to show what their objects created or possess.
It calls invoking besides God beings that cannot answer until the Day of Resurrection the furthest error.
It states that, when people are gathered, the invoked beings become enemies and reject their worship.
The named female deities supply a concrete instance of the rival objects rejected throughout the focus's theme.
It reduces the alleged deities to names with no divine authority, closely paralleling the invalidity of worshiped objects.
It commands that no one be invoked together with God, supplying the categorical contrary rule.
